headline: Shorts: the feed stopped expanding us on Oct 10. Shorts-feed views per week went 3,518 (Sep 28 wk) → 1,758 (Oct 5) → 336 (Oct 12), and channel views fell to 795 in the Oct 12 week, the lowest since Aug 17. The mechanism is not a smaller audition: every short since Oct 10 still got its normal 20–80 feed views on day 0, still sits in the SHORTS traffic source, and median avg-view% is 64% (higher than September's 45%). What changed is that 0 of 16 auditions expanded; since Sep 1 the base rate was 14 of 45 shorts clearing 250 views (31%), so 0/16 is a 0.3% event. The 16 are the Ep 18 slate (1/day, 0 of 6 before the two-a-day cadence started) plus Ep 19 (2/day since Oct 16); the common factor is the slate: concept and AI-insider lines ('Claude Just Horcruxed Himself' 16, '36 Coin Flips' 16, 'Justin Drake' 33, 'One Guy at Cloudflare' 60) where every 4-digit short on the channel was an absurd, physical or money line ('A Kid's Savings at 100x Leverage' 1,022, 'Bring a $5 wrench' 901, 'A Microphone That Smells Like Fish' 911, 'Cigarettes and Gambling' 510, 'wife beater' 710). Long-form: Ep 19 launched at the channel's best CTR (3.73% on 1,018 impressions) and 239 views; Ep 18's 418 views are 81 engaged views plus feed autoplays — YouTube has counted a view from the first frame since 2026-08-24, and engaged views per episode have been flat at 40–120 since June (Ep 12 121, Ep 16 98, Ep 18 81, Ep 19 51), so the raw-view growth since Ep 12 was never real; every study conclusion survives excluding the four autoplay-heavy episodes. Subs 26 → 31 since 9/19, zero lost. The perp-first structure (Ep 15–19) is graded: Ep 15 cleared the 20% target at the 10% mark (24.6%), Ep 16–19 did not (17.4 / 14.3 / 16.2 / 15.7). The new cross-episode study (analytics/study/study.md, 382 chapters, 19 curves) says why: the perp pick placed in the first third is the lowest-scoring content-position cell on the show (vs_typ 0.28), the first tenth of runtime loses 10.6%/min vs 0.9–2.9% after, long topic blocks hold better than short ones, and no host is better or worse than another — mechanism explainers are the floor and stakes/stories are the ceiling regardless of who talks.

production.title: Shorts feed stopped expanding us Oct 10: 0 of 16 auditions broke out vs a 31% base rate — re-pick the slate, pause two-a-day
production.evidence: Shorts-feed views by week: Sep 14 3,776 · Sep 21 1,335 · Sep 28 3,518 · Oct 5 1,758 · Oct 12 336. Per-short day-0 feed views since Oct 10: 65, 53, 83, 7, 28, 13, 48, 4, 13, 43 (median ~40; September median ~50) — the audition still runs. Every one is in the SHORTS traffic source (not a classification problem). Engaged/views ratio on the misses 18–33%, same as September misses. Median avg-view% of the Oct 12-week shorts 64% vs 45% for the Sep 14 week — retention is not the problem. Breakouts (≥250 views) since Sep 1: 14 of 45 before Oct 10, 0 of 16 after. Ep 18 slate at 1/day was already 0 of 6 before the Ep 19 two-a-day run started Oct 16. The one browse-distributed short this month, 'Their brains just break if your email isn't gmail.com', got 2,047 impressions at 0.54% CTR (fruit fly: 821 at 8.9%).
production.recommendation: Three moves. (1) Hold the remaining Ep 19 schedule (5 left through Oct 23) but do not add more two-a-day; back to 1/day. (2) Next batch is 5–7 clips picked by the winner template only: an absurd physical premise or a dollar figure, a host's face reacting in frame 1, no model names, no protocol names, no segment jargon. The 'Which AI picked our trade?' / 'SaaS-less' class is what has been failing. (3) Cross-check the same clips on TikTok (episodes/tiktok.md): if TikTok views also flattened on the Ep 18/19 batches it is the slate; if TikTok held, it is YouTube distribution and we wait it out. Title lesson from the gmail short: a quote with no hook noun got 2k browse impressions and converted 0.5%; browse titles need the object in the first three words.

production.title: Ep 19 launched at the channel's best CTR (3.73%) with a concrete-object title; keep that title shape
production.evidence: Launch impressions / CTR: Ep 16 2,758 / 2.5%, Ep 17 974 / 2.98%, Ep 18 2,070 / 2.85%, Ep 19 1,018 / 3.73% ('They Hid a SIM Card Inside a Crypto Wallet. $102M Gone.'). Ep 19 day 0/1 views 57 / 94 (Ep 18: 55 / 66 / 141). Captions + 15 tags were patched on launch day (10/16) after the manual upload revoked the force-ssl token again.
production.recommendation: Title = physical object + what happened + dollar figure. Ep 19 is the fourth episode in a row to clear 2.5% once the title carried a number; the Ep 10 (0.58%) and Ep 14 (1.55%) misses were abstractions. Thumbnail text 'THEY BUGGED THE WALLET' passed the shrink test; keep three-word thumbnails.
production.status_note: closed 10/20: measured inside the launch window.

production.title: Cross-episode study shipped: analytics/study/study.md (382 chapters × 19 retention curves, speaker + topic + length)
production.evidence: episode_study.py joins each retention curve to the episode's chapter table and speaker-attributed SRT (14 of 19 episodes have speakers). Key numbers: first tenth of runtime loses 10.6%/min vs 0.9–2.9% for the rest; perp pick in the first third vs_typ 0.28 (worst cell); topic blocks 10+ min vs_typ 0.43 vs <3 min 0.36; dominant speaker Tyler 0.41 / Chris 0.40 / Jackson 0.38 with overlapping CIs; worst chapter per episode is a mechanism explainer in 12 of 19 episodes.
production.recommendation: Re-run it after every episode (two commands, in study.md). The recording items below are now graded against it instead of against single-episode reads.

production.title: Not bots: YouTube counts a view from the first frame since 2026-08-24 — engaged views per episode have been flat at 40–120 since June; report engaged views from now on
production.evidence: YouTube's Aug 24 change counts feed autoplays as views (TechCrunch 8/17, vidIQ, RouteNote); the old definition is 'engaged views'. Analytics API per episode (views → engaged): Ep 1–11 85–100% engaged (37–127 each); Ep 12 306 → 121; Ep 13 225 → 82; Ep 14 215 → 70; Ep 15 163 → 64; Ep 16 400 → 98; Ep 17 194 → 42; Ep 18 417 → 81; Ep 19 151 → 51. Jackson's Studio reads match the autoplay story: Ep 18 5.5% US, <0.1% regular viewers; Ep 16 46% US; Ep 12 16% US, 90% mobile; subscriber-sourced views carry only 31–33% of watch time in all three. Ep 3 (293, 100% engaged, US 36% + CA/AU/UK, all 35–44 male) was a genuine shared launch, not an anomaly. avg_view_pct is not comparable across Aug 24 (denominator now includes autoplay starts) — minutes per engaged view is: 4–11 before, 4–6 after.
production.recommendation: Done: yt_pull.py now pulls engagedViews per video; the report shows an Engaged column, an 'engaged episode views' KPI and a regime note. From here: launches are graded on engaged views and minutes per engaged view, never raw views. The honest read: the show's real audience per episode is the same 40–120 people it was in July, and the growth story in raw views since Ep 12 was never real.
production.status_note: closed 10/20: Studio reads on Ep 3/12/16/18 + Aug 24 counting change; 'bot' retracted.

recording.title: Perp-first opening graded on five episodes: 1 pass, 4 fails — move the perp pick to the first break (~minute 8–10) and open on the marquee's victim and number
recording.evidence: 10% mark (target ≥20%): Ep 15 24.6 (pass), Ep 16 17.4, Ep 17 14.3, Ep 18 16.2, Ep 19 15.7. Ep 18 perp 1:38–6:03 took retention 32% → 16% (vs_typ 0.24); Ep 19 perp 1:15–4:20 29% → 16% (0.41); Ep 15's 2.5-min perp held 34% → 27%. Pooled across 19 episodes, perp chapters in the first third average vs_typ 0.28 — the worst content × position cell on the show — while perp checks and tallies later average 0.37 and the two best perp chapters ever recorded were late payoffs (Ep 8 'GPT-5.6 goes long XRP' 32:44 at 0.91; Ep 5 'We got a perp!' 50:45 at 0.59). Study §1–2. With the four autoplay-heavy episodes (3/12/16/18) excluded as a sensitivity check, early perp softens to vs_typ 0.34 but stays the lowest substantive cell; Ep 17 and 19 (clean) failed the 20% target at 14.3 and 15.5.
recording.recommendation: Welcome ≤40 s, then straight into the marquee with the victim and the number in the first sentence (Ep 19 had it: '$102M, a SIM card inside the wallet' — but it ran at 5:43 after 4.5 min of perp). First break at ~8–10 min = perp pick with the board on screen. Keep the halftime check and the final tally where they are; they score. Grade on Ep 20's 6:00 mark vs the Ep 15–19 range 14–24%.

recording.title: Stop cutting for length — long topic blocks hold better than short ones and loss inside a chapter does not climb with minutes
recording.evidence: Topic blocks (consecutive same-category chapters): 10+ min vs_typ 0.43 (CI 0.39–0.48), 6–10 min 0.40, 3–6 min 0.36, <3 min 0.36 (CI 0.32–0.40). Loss per minute inside a chapter: minutes 1–6 run 1.7–3.5%/min, minutes 7–15 ~0–2%. Within-episode regression: longer chapters have lower hazard (−0.015 per SD, CI −0.026…−0.006). Bitcoin/L2 is the longest-running category (median block 6.1 min) and the best (0.43). Study §3, §5.
recording.recommendation: Drop the ≤8-minute explainer cap and the 45–55-minute target as retention rules; nothing in 19 episodes shows a block that ran too long. Cut a chapter when it has no stakes, never because it crossed a clock. Edit-side: merge beats rather than chop; fewer, longer chapters in the sheet too.

recording.title: No host is the problem — mechanism explainers are the floor and stakes/stories the ceiling, for all three of you
recording.evidence: Dominant-speaker vs_typ: Tyler 0.41 (n=89), Chris 0.40 (66), Jackson 0.38 (65), CIs overlap; every speaker-share, crosstalk, words-per-minute and longest-turn coefficient on vs_typ has a CI spanning zero (n=220). Worst chapter per episode is a how-it-works/product explainer in 12 of 19: 'How Spark works' 0.11, 'How a Lightning channel works' 0.17, 'Q-Day vs a classical break' 0.18, 'Is SaaS still viable' 0.13, 'Instinct switched a utility plan' 0.07, 'Tyler's $10K prompt → SaaS' 0.04, 'The standards war' 0.07. Best per episode is a person with a loss or a thing: 'Coldcard catastrophe' 0.57, 'emergency fund went into Stretch' 0.84, 'Gavin the fruit fly' 0.60, 'Spark operators see everything' 0.75, 'You slip up once and it undoes years' 0.62, 'Instinct update: a tennis tournament every week' 0.67. Tyler is on both lists. Study §4.
recording.recommendation: Every explainer block opens with a victim, a number, or the host who got burned, inside its first 60 s — then the mechanism. Lightning (Ep 19) had the material: lead with the tester who spent 80,000 sats to recover 20,000, then the HTLCs. The industry-state block also still scores 0.13–0.25 when it runs after minute 20 (Ep 19 SaaS, 20:42–34:26), so 'after minute 20' did not fix it; stakes-first is the fix, not the slot.

recording.title: Banter and prop bits belong after the first third
recording.evidence: banter_personal in the first third: vs_typ 0.24, 21.6%/min loss (n=6: Rubik's cubes + beers at Ep 17 3:30 scored 0.18; Ep 11 gorilla arc; Ep 2 housekeeping 0.14). Placed later: 0.50 (n=10) — the best thing on the show (Ep 16 cult story 0.80, Ep 7 freestyle 0.61). The [rec] prop/animal/live-dollar experiment ran once (Ep 17 cubes) in the first third and produced a 409-view feed short, not a browse hit (179 impressions, 0.56%). Study §2.
recording.recommendation: Keep doing the bits; schedule them after the first payoff (minute 10+). The on-mic prop experiment stays open with that placement.

recording.title: Cold opens remain solved; the 0:30–2:00 collapse is the same on every curve regardless of what follows
recording.evidence: At 0:32: Ep 15 90%, Ep 16 84%, Ep 17 79%, Ep 18 81%, Ep 19 71% (Ep 19's 35-s three-beat open is the shortest and lowest of the five). All 19 curves lose 40–70 points between 0:30 and 2:00. 1:05 → 6:00 keep ratio median 0.41 across episodes; perp-first eps 0.31–0.52.
recording.recommendation: Keep 3–5 beats in ≤45 s with the finale tease. Ep 19's open at 35 s with three beats read thin at 0:32 — four beats is the sweet spot on the record (Ep 14 88%, Ep 17 79%).

experiments: [prod] Ep 20 launch graded on ENGAGED views and minutes per engaged view (Ep 15–19: 42–98 engaged, 4.1–6.3 min each). Raw views are a feed-autoplay counter since Aug 24.

[prod] Ep 20 shorts: 5–7 clips, winner template only (physical/absurd premise or dollar figure, face in frame 1, no model/protocol names), 1/day. Pass = ≥2 of the batch clear 250 views within 3 days (September rate was ~1 in 3).
[prod] Shorts slate vs distribution: pull TikTok views for the Ep 18/19 clips from episodes/tiktok.md. If TikTok also flattened on those batches → slate; if not → YouTube distribution.
[rec] Ep 20 structure: welcome ≤40 s → marquee with victim + number in the first sentence → perp pick as the first break at ~8–10 min. Pass = retention at 6:00 ≥ 20% (Ep 15–19 range 14–24%).
[rec] Ep 20: every explainer block opens with a victim/number/burned host inside 60 s. Measure the block's vs_typ vs the 0.11–0.18 of 'How Spark works' / 'How a Lightning channel works' / 'Q-Day'.
[rec] Prop/animal/live-dollar bit, placed after minute 10. Measure its chapter vs_typ (early placements scored 0.18–0.24) and whether its short reaches browse (≥300 impressions).
